AGENDA
CITY OF AZUSA
REGULAR MEETING
OF THE CITY COUNCIL,
THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO
THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, AND
THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
AZUSA AUDITORIUM
213 EAST FOOTHILL BOULEVARD
AZUSA, CA 91702
MONDAY, NOVEMBER 5, 2018
06:30 P.M.
Closed Session
7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting/Ceremonial
AZUSA CITY COUNCIL
JOSEPH ROMERO ROCHA
MAYOR
ROBERT GONZALES
MAYOR PRO TEM
EDWARD J. ALVAREZ
COUNCIL MEMBER
URIEL E. MACIAS
COUNCIL MEMBER
ANGEL A. CARILLO
COUNCIL MEMBER
06:30 P.M.
1.
Call to Order
2.
Roll Call
CEREMONIAL
1.
The following Police Officers will be sworn into office: Christopher Grant, Captain; Robert Chivas, Lieutenant; Robert Landeros, Lieutenant; Seth Chapman, Sergeant; Fernando Vasconcelos, Sergeant; Trevor Benson, Corporal; Richard Martinez, Corporal; Jonathan Rush, Corporal; Jared Bird, Officer; Benjamin Cypher, Officer; Matthew DeCaro, Officer; Denise Ferrari, Officer; Samantha Hedrick, Officer; Michael Munoz, Officer; and Steven Rodriguez, Officer.
CLOSED SESSION
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR CLOSED SESSION
Prior to going into closed session the City Council will convene in the Auditorium serving as Council Chambers to take public comment on the closed session items only. General public comment will be provided for during the regular portion of the meeting beginning at 7:30 P.M.
1.
CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS - Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54957.6. City Negotiator: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager and Tanya Bragg, Director of Human Resources & Risk Management
Organizations: SEIU (Service Employees International Union- Local 721), ACEA (Azusa City Employees Association), AMMA (Azusa Middle Management Association), APOA (Azusa Police Officers Association), CAPP (Civilian Association of Police Personnel), and APMA (Azusa Police Middle Management Association)
JOINT CITY/SUCCESSOR AGENCY ITEM
2.
CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS - Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54956.8. City/ Agency Negotiators: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager/Executive Director and Kurt E. Christiansen, Director of Economic and Community Development
Property Address: Block 37: 624 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-914); 622 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-912, 913); 618 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-903, 904); 612 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-905); 610 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-902); 604 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-907); 600 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-906).
Negotiating Parties: All potential purchasers
Under Negotiation: Price and Terms
7:30 P.M. - REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.ci.azusa.ca.us. Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after will not be accepted.
A.
PRELIMINARY BUSINESS
1.
Call to Order
2.
Roll Call
3.
Flag Salute
4.
Invocation – Pastor Daniel Simonson, Christbridge Immanuel Church
5.
Closed Session Report by the City Attorney
B.
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items within the subject matter jurisdiction of the council/agency board that are not listed on this agenda or are listed on this agenda as an item other than a public hearing item. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the
city council/agency board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the council/agency board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. The council/agency board will respond after public comment has been received. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments shall be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.
C.
REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL
D.
SCHEDULED ITEMS - None
E.
CONSENT CALENDAR
The Consent Calendar adopting the printed recommended actions will be enacted with one vote. If Councilmembers or Staff wish to address any item on the Consent Calendar
individually, it will be considered under SPECIAL CALL ITEMS.
1.
MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF OCTOBER 15, 2018 AND SPECIAL MEETING OF OCTOBER 22, 2018.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve minutes as written.
E-1 - Minutes - October 15, 2018, Regular Meeting and October 22, 2018, Special Meeting
2.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING PAYMENTS OF WARRANTS BY THE CITY DATED OCTOBER 10, 2018 THROUGH OCTOBER 31, 2018.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2018-C64 allowing certain claims and demands and specifying the funds out of which the same are to be paid.
E-2 - Warrant Register, 10.10.2018-10.31.2018
3.
HUMAN RESOURCES ACTION ITEMS.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the Personnel Action Requests in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules Section 5.7.5 and applicable Memorandum of Understanding(s).
E-3 - Staff Report - Human Resources Action Items
4.
APPROVE A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH FOOTHILL TRANSIT FOR THE RELOCATION OF THEIR SERVICE UTILITY BOX LOCATED ADJACENT TO THE FUTURE A-2 MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT PROJECT AT AZUSA AVENUE AND NINTH STREET.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Authorize the City Manager to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Foothill Transit for the relocation of the Foothill Transit main switchgear on the Foothill Transit busway; and authorize the City Manager to execute, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.
E-4 - Staff Report - MOU with Foothill Transit
5.
GRANT AGREEMENT FROM CA OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY FOR THE “SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM” (STEP) 2018-2019. GRANT NUMBER PT19005.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve Resolution No. 2018-C65 accepting a grant in the amount of $95,000.00 (for hourly wages at an overtime rate) from the California Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) to conduct DUI Saturation Patrols to apprehend drunk drivers, Warrant Service Operations and other related traffic programs; and authorize the Mayor to execute the grant agreement.
E-5 - Staff Report - OTS Grant 18-19
6.
AWARD CONTRACT FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) SIDEWALK AND ADA IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT NO. 601965-18 LOCATED WITHIN THE AREA BOUNDED BY FIFTH STREET ON THE NORTH, FOURTH STREET ON THE SOUTH, ORANGE AVENUE ON THE WEST, AND ALAMEDA AVENUE ON THE EAST.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Award a construction contract in the amount of $95,368, which includes 10% for contingency for potential change orders as needed, to Ruiz Concrete and Paving, Inc. for the Sidewalk and ADA Improvements Project No. 601965-18; and authorize the City Manager to execute a contract, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.
E-6 - Staff Report - CDBG Sidewalk and ADA Improvements Project
7.
CITY TREASURER’S STATEMENT OF CASH AND INVESTMENT BALANCES FOR THE MONTH OF AUGUST 2018.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive, review, and file the City Treasurer’s Report for the month of August 2018.
E-7 - Staff Report - Treasurers Report 08-2018
8.
AWARD A CONTRACT FOR THE AZUSA LIBRARY AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT (ADA) COMPLIANT RESTROOM RETROFIT AND IMPROVEMENT PROJECT [COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROJECT (CDBG) 601863-17].
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Award a contract for a total not-to-exceed amount of $250,555, which includes a 10% contingency for potential change orders as needed, to Corral Construction & Development, Inc., for the Azusa Library ADA Compliant Restroom Retrofit and Improvement Project (Community Development Block Grant Project 601863-17); and authorize the City Manager to execute a contract, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.
E-8 - Staff Report - Library ADA Restroom Award
9.
RELEASE OF BONDS FOR TRACTS 54057-15 AND 54057-17 IN THE ROSEDALE COMMUNITY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Release the Performance Bond in the amount of $578,535, the Labor and Materials Bond in the amount of $578,535 and the Monument Bond in the amount of $13,800 for Tract 54057-15; and release the Performance Bond in the amount of $363,529, the Labor and Materials Bond in the amount of $363,529, and the Monument Bond in the amount of $7,000 for Tract 54057-17.
E-9 - Staff Report - Tract 54057-15 and 17 Bond Release
10.
APPROVE THE IMPROVEMENT PLANS FOR THE VERNON AVENUE FROM GLADSTONE STREET TO SANTA FE AVENUE PAVEMENT REHABILITATION PROJECT AND AUTHORIZE STAFF TO SOLICIT A NOTICE OF INVITING BIDS.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the project plans; and authorize staff to solicit a Notice of Inviting Bids for the Vernon Avenue Pavement Rehabilitation Project.
E-10 - Staff Report - Vernon Ave Pavement Rehabilitation Project
11.
CLASS SPECIFICATION REVISION – SENIOR PLANNER.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the revised classification specification for the position of Senior Planner.
E-11 - Staff Report - Classification Specification Revision - Senior Planner
12.
PURCHASE OF UNDERGROUND COPPER CABLE.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the issuance of a purchase order to Wesco Distribution in an amount not to exceed $254,406.
E-12 - Staff Report - Purchase of Underground Copper Cable
F.
SUCCESSOR AGENCY RELATED BUSINESS.
1.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING PAYMENT OF WARRANTS BY THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY DATED SEPTEMBER 28, 2018 THROUGH OCTOBER 31, 2018.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2018-R16 allowing certain claims and demands to be paid out of Successor Agency Funds.
F-1 - Successor Agency Warrant Register, 9.28.2018-10.31.2018
G.
ADJOURNMENT
UPCOMING MEETINGS:
November 19, 2018, 6:30 p.m. Ceremonial/Closed Session, 7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting
December 3, 2018, 6:30 p.m. Ceremonial/Closed Session, 7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in a city meeting, please contact the City Clerk at 626-812-5229. Notification three (3) working days prior to the meeting when special services are needed will assist staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide access to the meeting.

CITY OF AZUSA
  MINUTES OF THE CITY COUNCIL, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY
  TO THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY,
  THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 5, 2018 – 6:30 P.M.

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in regular session at the above date and time in the Azusa Auditorium located
at 213 E. Foothill Boulevard, Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 6:34 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo. Councilmember Carrillo arrived at 6:36 p.m., after roll call.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, MACIAS, CARRILLO, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.
Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Martinez, Chief of Police Hunt, Director of Human Resources &
Risk Management Bragg, Neighborhood Services Coordinator Quiroz, and Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

CEREMONIAL

The following Police Officers were sworn into office:

Christopher Grant, Captain; Robert Chivas, Lieutenant; Seth Chapman, Sergeant; Fernando Vasconcelos, Sergeant;
Trevor Benson, Corporal; Jonathan Rush, Corporal; Jared Bird, Officer; Benjamin Cypher, Officer; Matthew DeCaro,
Officer; Denise Ferrari, Officer; Samantha Hedrick, Officer; and Michael Munoz, Officer.

PUBLIC COMMENT

None given.

CLOSED SESSION

The City Council recessed to closed session at 7:11 P.M. to discuss the following:

1. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS - Pursuant to California Government Code, Section
  54957.6.
  City Negotiator: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager and Tanya Bragg, Director of Human Resources & Risk
  Management
  Organizations: SEIU (Service Employees International Union- Local 721), ACEA (Azusa City Employees
  Association), AMMA (Azusa Middle Management Association), APOA (Azusa Police Officers
  Association), CAPP (Civilian Association of Police Personnel), and APMA (Azusa Police Middle
  Management Association)

JOINT CITY/SUCCESSOR AGENCY ITEM

2. CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS - Pursuant to California Government Code,
  Section 54956.8.

  City/ Agency Negotiators: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager/Executive Director and Kurt E. Christiansen, Director of
  Economic and Community Development
  Property Address:  Block 37: 624 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-914); 622 N. San Gabriel Avenue
  (APN 8611-004-912, 913); 618 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-903, 904); 612
  N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-905); 610 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-
  004-902); 604 N. San Gabriel Avenue (APN 8611-004-907); 600 N. San Gabriel Avenue
  (APN 8611-004-906).
  Negotiating Parties:  All potential purchasers
  Under Negotiation:  Price and Terms

REGULAR SESSION
 Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 7:46 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo, City Treasurer Vasquez.

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Martinez, Chief of Police Hunt, Director of Public Works/City
Engineer Bobadilla, Director of Utilities Robledo, Director of Finance Johnson, Director of Recreation and Family
Services Carpenter, Police Captain Grant, Neighborhood Services Coordinator Quiroz, and Chief Deputy City Clerk
Garcia.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the following family members of Ms. Maria Concepcion Gomez, Lifelong Azusa
Resident: Mr. Wenses Orrosquieta, Ms. Liliana Orrosquieta, Ms. Mariah Orrosquieta, and Mr. Abel Orrosquieta.

The invocation was given by Pastor Daniel Simonson, Christbridge Immanuel Church.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Council reconvened at 7:46 P.M.; City Attorney Martinez announced the following regarding Closed Session:
All members of the Council were present; Item 1: City Council heard a presentation, provided additional direction, no
further reportable action; Item 2: Item was not discussed and will be placed on a future agenda.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Mr. Hector Elizalde, representative of Congress Woman Napolitano, announced the 4th Annual Congressional Prayer
Breakfast on November 8, 2018; and reminded everyone of the importance of voting.

Ms. Diana Williams encouraged everyone to vote, and provided information on how to find your polling location.

Mr. Adrian Greer thanked Azusa Unified School Board candidates for their hard work and respect; and encouraged
everyone to vote.

Mr. Jorge V. Rosales inquired about the range of bid amounts received for the Sidewalk and ADA Improvements Project
in Item E-6; and inquired about the disqualification of the two lowest bidders for the Library Restroom Improvement
Project in Item E-8.

Director of Public Works/City Engineer responded to the inquiry regarding the Sidewalk and ADA Improvements Project
stating that project bid amounts can vary due to federal requirements, some contractors lack experience and therefore use
additional dollars to comply with those requirements. In response to the inquiry regarding the Library Restroom
Improvement Project, he stated that the CDC governs the City’s CDBG funds and certain requirements must be met, the
two lowest bidders did not meet those requirements and were disqualified.

REPORTS, UPDATES AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Gonzalez provided an update to the previously held discussion regarding the maintenance of City medians
stating that Staff reviewed the current contract and the contractor was found to be in compliance with the contract
requirements; Staff will work on watering and reseeding the medians while maintaining the State’s water restrictions and
will present long-term median beautification options to the Council at a later date; and announced that the Finance
Department received a Certificate of Achievement in for Excellence in Financial Reporting from the Government Finance
Officers Association and commended Director of Finance Johnson for her work.

Mayor Pro-Tem Gonzales reminded everyone to exercise their right to vote.

Councilmember Carrillo encouraged everyone to vote.

Councilmember Alvarez wished good luck to all candidates; wished a Happy Veteran’s Day to everyone; and announced
that the Eureka Café is now open.

Councilmember Macias expressed his appreciation of the follow-up on the median issue; thanked Director of Finance
Johnson for her work; inquired about parking enforcement on street sweeping days; requested anupdate on Block 36 by
the developer; inquired about the possibility of a Lighting and Landscape Assessment; encouraged everyone to vote;
announced the EDDY awards on November 8, 2018; thanked Water Board Member Al Contreras, Fire Chief Jim
Enriquez, and City Treasurer Art Vasquez for their constant attendance at the Council Meetings; and inquired about
setting up a Goals Working Session with City Manager Gonzalez.

Chief of Police Hunt stated that parking enforcement patrols prior to the street sweeper arriving to ensure cars are not
parked on the streets.
PAGE TWO – 11/5/2018
Mayor Rocha announced that the meeting would be adjourned in memory Mr. Lawrence Martinez, Jr., Ms. Maria
Concepcion Gomez, and Mr. Jesse Barajas, Life Long Azusa Residents and Mr. Miguel Angel Oliva Martinez, Longtime
 Azusa Resident. He encouraged everyone to vote; reminded residents about the winter watering schedule; he announced
the following events: November 7 – On the Move Program at the Senior Center, November 8 – Veteran’s Day Ceremony
at the Senior Center, November 8 – Saluting Our Veterans at Citrus College, November 8 – Los Angeles County
Economic Development Corporation EDDY Awards, November 10 – Be-A-Walker at Veterans Park, November 11 –
Veteran’s Day Ceremony at City Hall; and asked everyone to keep the service men and women in their daily prayers.

In response to a request by the Council, Director of Public Works/City Engineer Bobadilla provided an update on the
Iconic A stating that the Artist is working on having the A delivered to Azusa.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

None.

CONSENT CALENDAR: Moved by Councilmember Carrillo, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem Gonzales and carried by the
following vote of the Council, to approve Consent Calendar Items E-1 to E-12. Councilmember Carrillo abstained from
Item E-6 only, due to the proximity of his property.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  COUNCILMEMBERS: CARRILLO (Item E-6 only)
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

1. The minutes of the Regular Meeting of October 15, 2018 and Special Meeting of October 22, 2018 were approved as
  written.

2. Resolution No. 2018-C64 was adopted and entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND
  DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

3. The Human Resources Action Items, in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules Section 5.75 and
  applicable Memorandum of Understanding(s), were approved as follows:
  Merit Increase and/or Regular Appointment: R. Arevalo, G. Enriquez, J. Kroner, E. Vazquez
  Flexible Staffing Promotion: R. Nodarse
  Reclassification: J. M. Munoz
  Separation: A. Clark, X. Torres.

4. A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Foothill Transit for the relocation of the Foothill Transit main
  switchgear on the Foothill Transit busway was approved; and the City Manager was authorized to execute the MOU
  on behalf of the City.

5. Resolution No. 2018-C65, accepting a grant in the amount of $95,000.00 (for hourly wages at an overtime rate) from
  the Office of Traffic Safety to conduct DUI Saturation Patrols to apprehend drunk drivers, Warrant Service
  Operations and other related traffic programs was adopted and entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A GRANT
  AGREEMENT WITH THE CALIFORNIA OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY (OTS) FOR THE “SELECTIVE
  TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (STEP)” 2018-2019 GRANT NO. PT19005

  and the Mayor was authorized to execute the grant agreement on behalf of the City.

6. A construction contract in the amount of $95,368, which includes 10% for contingency for potential change orders as
  needed, was awarded to Ruiz Concrete and Paving, Inc. for the Sidewalk and ADA Improvements Project No.
  601965-18; and the City Manager was authorized to execute the contract on behalf of the City.

7. The City Treasurer’s Report for the month of August 2018 was received, reviewed, and filed.

8. A contract for a total not-to-exceed amount of $250,555, which includes a 10% contingency for potential change
  orders as needed, was awarded to Corral Construction & Development, Inc., for the Azusa Library ADA Compliant
  Restroom Retrofit and Improvement Project No. 601863-17; and the City Manager was authorized to execute the
  contract on behalf of the City.

9. The Performance Bond in the amount of $578,535, the Labor and Materials Bond in the amount of $578,535, and the
  Monument Bond in the amount of $13,800 for Tract 564057-15, were released; and the Performance Bond in the
  amount of $363,529, the Labor and Materials Bond in the amount of $363,529, and the Monument Bond in the
  amount of $7,000, for Tract 54057-17, were released.

10. The improvement plans for the Vernon Avenue from Gladstone Street to Santa Fe Avenue Pavement Rehabilitation
  Project were approved; and Staff was authorized to solicit a Notice of Inviting Bids for the Project.

11. The revised classification specification for the position of Senior Planner was approved.

PAGE THREE – 11/5/2018

12. The issuance of a purchase order to Wesco Distribution in the amount not-to-exceed $254,406 for the purchase of
  Underground Copper Cable was approved.
 SUCCESSOR AGENCY RELATED BUSINESS

RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING PAYMENT OF WARRANTS BY THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY DATED
SPETEMBER 28, 2018 THROUGH OCTOBER 31, 2018

Agency Member Alvarez offered Resolution No. 2018-R16 entitled:

A RESOLUTION OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY OF THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY OF THE CITY
OF AZUSA ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS TO BE PAID OUT OF SUCCESSOR AGENCY
FUNDS

Moved by Agency Member Gonzales, seconded by Agency Member Carrillo, and carried by unanimous vote of the
Agency to adopt Resolution No. 2018-R16.

AYES:  AGENCY MEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE

ADJOURNMENT:

The meeting was adjourned by consensus of the City Council in memory of Mr. Lawrence Martinez, Jr., Ms. Maria
Concepcion Gomez, and Mr. Jesse Barajas, Lifelong Azusa Residents, and Mr. Miguel Angel Oliva Martinez, Longtime
Azusa Resident.

TIME OF ADJOURNMENT: 8:30 P.M.

__________________________________________
CITY CLERK

NEXT RESOLUTION NO. 2018-C66 (City)
NEXT ORDINANCE NO. 2018-05
NEXT RESOLUTION NO. 2018-R17 (Former Redevelopment Agency)

NEXT MEETINGS: November 19, 2018 and December 3, 2018.
